subject.title: [Feature] Prime-number default scheduling for HEARTBEAT / cron “every” + deterministic per-agent phase jitter (anti top-of-hour spikes)

question: Should OpenClaw add public phase, jitter, or prime-cadence controls for cron `every` schedules, and if so should that contract also expose heartbeat knobs or keep heartbeat phase spreading internal?
rationale: The remaining work is not a broken existing contract; it adds public scheduling semantics and config/API surface in an area where repository policy treats config/default changes as compatibility-sensitive.

options.title: Design narrow cron every phase/stagger contract
options.body: Add one explicit interval-schedule anti-herd contract covering schema, CLI, persistence, docs, and upgrade behavior before implementation.

options.title: Keep every fixed
options.body: Preserve current anchored `every` semantics and rely on heartbeat phase spreading plus cron-expression stagger for anti-herd protection.

options.title: Adopt broader prime mode
options.body: Accept a larger product surface with prime cadence transforms and explicit heartbeat/cron phase controls, including migration and observability requirements.

recommendation.title: Design narrow cron every phase/stagger contract
recommendation.body: Add one explicit interval-schedule anti-herd contract covering schema, CLI, persistence, docs, and upgrade behavior before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the current cron-expression stagger surface and are the best available routing candidate for the remaining cron scheduling product boundary.
